questions.question: On supported Python versions, how can a slotted attrs class use a functools.cached_property declared on that class without an instance __dict__? Explain what attrs changes on the class, how the first successful read and later reads work even for a frozen instance, whether a failing computation is cached, and how unrelated missing attributes reach a class-defined or inherited __getattr__.

criteria.description: During slotted-class construction, attrs detects cached_property descriptors, saves their functions, removes the descriptors, adds their names to the slot names, and installs a generated __getattr__ to compute them.

For a missing cached-property slot, the generated getter invokes the saved function and stores its result in the slot using a bound object.__setattr__, bypassing frozen assignment restrictions; subsequent ordinary slot reads retrieve the stored result without invoking __getattr__ again.
The result is stored only after the property function returns; an exception propagates without installing a cached result, so a later read can attempt computation again.

Unknown names are delegated directly to the original class-defined __getattr__ when present. Otherwise the generated fallback tries the superclass attribute lookup and, on AttributeError, calls an inherited __getattr__ if present or reraises when absent.

questions.question: How does resolve_types use globalns, localns, and include_extras to resolve field types, and how do its normal field lookup and explicit attribs path differ? Without attribs it uses fields(cls); with attribs it uses the supplied sequence instead. Only fields whose names appear in the hints have their type replaced, using object.__setattr__ to bypass frozen metadata; the original class is returned.

The cache marker stores the resolved class itself. A later call on that same class skips work, including changed namespaces, while a subclass inheriting a base's marker still resolves because the marker is not equal to the subclass.

Exceptions from get_type_hints propagate without being caught, and the success marker is only assigned after hint resolution and field updates, so a failed first resolution does not mark that class as resolved.

questions.question: During shell completion, how does Click choose whether the current command, an option awaiting values, or a positional argument handles the incomplete word? Explain normalization of a standalone equals sign and an option=value word, the role of the -- marker in option-name completion, which options count as awaiting values, and when a positional argument remains eligible before falling back to the command.

criteria.description: A standalone incomplete equals sign becomes an empty incomplete value. An incomplete word containing equals and beginning with a recognized option prefix is split at its first equals; its option name is appended to the complete arguments and the value becomes the incomplete word.

Before looking for incomplete parameter values, a prefix-looking incomplete word is assigned to the current command for option-name completion if -- is absent from the completed arguments. Presence of -- disables this early option-name branch.

Options awaiting values take precedence over positional arguments. Flags and count options are excluded; the helper scans backward through at most the option nargs completed tokens, remembers a prefix-looking token, and treats the option as incomplete only when that token matches one of its option names. The first qualifying parameter is selected.

Next the first eligible Argument is selected: variadic nargs=-1, a value not sourced from the command line, or a multi-value argument whose tuple/list has fewer than nargs entries. If none qualifies, completion falls back to the current command.

material_error_examples: A flag option is always eligible to complete a following value.
Any already-populated positional argument is ineligible, even if its value came only from a default.
Positional argument completion is selected before checking options awaiting values.
The -- marker has no effect on the early option-name completion branch.
An option=value incomplete word is always handed intact to command-name completion.

questions.question: How does Context.scope control the active context and resource cleanup when the same context is nested or cleanup=False? Explain when resources registered with with_resource and call_on_close are acquired or released, what current-context lookup sees inside and after a normally completed scope, and how close supports reuse. Assume cleanup handlers themselves do not raise.

criteria.description: Entering a scope pushes the context onto the active-context stack, so current-context lookup returns it; normal exit pops it and reveals the previous context. Ordinary lookup with no active context raises RuntimeError. Thread isolation and the optional silent lookup mode are not required.

Each entry increments the same context depth and each exit decrements it; automatic cleanup occurs only when the depth reaches zero, so an inner ordinary scope does not close resources still owned by an outer entry.

cleanup=False adds an extra depth increment around the normal context-manager entry and removes it in finally. The scope still pushes and pops the active context but its exit avoids close; the compensating decrement itself does not trigger cleanup.

with_resource enters the supplied context manager immediately through the ExitStack; call_on_close registers a deferred callback. close closes the stack, releasing registered resources and callbacks, then installs a fresh ExitStack for reuse. The with_resource return value is optional supporting detail.

questions.question: How can a command's help text contain prose reflowed to the formatter width, a literal multiline paragraph that is not reflowed, and a trailing section hidden from help? criteria.description: Command help is first cleaned with inspect.cleandoc and then cut off at the first form-feed character. The retained nonempty help is sent to write_text within the formatter indentation context; the trailing section is not formatted.

write_text passes formatter width and current indentation as both initial and subsequent indentation to wrap_text with paragraph preservation enabled. wrap_text expands tabs before constructing its wrapper. The formatter's final newline is optional supporting detail.

Empty lines flush accumulated paragraphs. For each paragraph, leading indentation is measured and removed from its first nonempty line; ordinary paragraph lines are joined with spaces and reflowed with that indentation added to the wrapper. Rendered paragraphs are joined by two newlines.

A paragraph whose first line, after stripping, is the backspace character (\b) is marked literal; that marker line is omitted and remaining lines are joined with newlines. It goes through indent_only rather than fill, preserving multiline layout without width-based reflow while adding the applicable indentation.

questions.question: On non-Windows platforms, how does Click's standard output helper handle ANSI styling for text when its color setting is explicit, inherited from an active context, or unspecified? Contrast this with nonempty bytes sent to a text stream with a binary buffer, including flush order, the fallback if no binary writer is found, and a call with no message and newline disabled.

criteria.description: For text, an explicit color argument wins; otherwise the active context color is used if there is one, or None is retained when there is no active context.

An explicit/resolved True preserves ANSI and False strips it. With color still None, ANSI is stripped only for a stream that is neither a TTY nor a recognized Jupyter kernel output stream; the text is then written and flushed.

Nonempty bytes bypass the text ANSI branch. Binary-writer lookup accepts the stream itself or its binary buffer; when found, the original stream is flushed before the bytes are written to and flushed on the binary writer, then the helper returns. If no binary writer is found, the original stream receives the raw bytes through write, followed by flush if that write succeeds.
With no message and newline disabled, the output remains empty: the helper flushes the selected stream and returns without writing or doing ANSI processing.

material_error_examples: Raw bytes are decoded and ANSI-stripped before being sent to a binary buffer.
An active context color=False overrides an explicit color=True argument.
Every non-TTY stream loses ANSI codes, including recognized Jupyter kernel output.
An empty no-newline call performs no flush.
A text stream without a binary writer causes bytes to be automatically converted to text.

questions.question: At the boundary where CliRunner.invoke calls cli.main, how does it represent a normal return and SystemExit(None), SystemExit(0), SystemExit with a nonzero integer, or SystemExit with a message string raised out of that call? Explain return_value, exit_code, exception, and exc_info where relevant, whether the string becomes captured output, and how catch_exceptions=False changes handling of SystemExit versus other Exception subclasses that escape cli.main.

criteria.description: A normal cli.main return is stored as return_value, with exit_code zero and exception and exc_info left as None; when main raises instead, return_value stays at its initialized None.
All SystemExit cases record sys.exc_info. A None code becomes zero; a zero code leaves Result.exception as None even though exc_info records the SystemExit.

A nonzero integer SystemExit keeps its code and stores the SystemExit as exception. For a message-string code, Result.exception still stores the SystemExit instance; the code is written to stdout with a newline and Result.exit_code becomes 1. The string remains the exception's code, and stdout is captured for the Result.

Other Exception subclasses are captured with exit_code 1, exception and exc_info when catch_exceptions is enabled, but re-raised when it is disabled. SystemExit has its own earlier handler and is still captured when catch_exceptions=False.

material_error_examples: catch_exceptions=False causes SystemExit to escape the runner.
SystemExit(0) is indistinguishable from a normal return because exc_info is None in both cases.
A SystemExit message string is only stored as return_value and is not printed.
The exit code from SystemExit(7) is always normalized to 1.

questions.question: How does LineDecoder preserve correct response lines when text chunks split a CRLF pair or split a line in the middle? Explain its treatment of other line separators and unfinished segments, what flush returns with pending text or a lone trailing carriage return, and how the synchronous and asynchronous response line iterators use it at end of input.

criteria.description: A trailing carriage return is removed from the current chunk and remembered, then prepended to the next chunk before splitting so that a cross-chunk CRLF is handled together.

The decoder uses str.splitlines and recognizes the listed newline characters, not just LF. It buffers chunks with no complete line, joins buffered text onto the next first segment, and withholds a final segment lacking a line terminator; yielded lines have no line separators.
flush returns no lines if neither buffer nor trailing CR remains; otherwise it emits one joined buffered line (an empty string for a lone pending CR with no text) and clears both pieces of state.
Both response line iterators consume their respective text iterator through a fresh LineDecoder, yield each decode result, and yield the final flush results once the text iterator ends.

material_error_examples: A carriage return at the end of a chunk immediately emits a line and the next LF emits a second empty line.
Only the LF character is recognized as a line separator.
An unterminated final line is discarded when response iteration finishes.

questions.question: When HTTPX query parameters contain several values for the same key, how can a caller append a value, replace all values for that key, or remove the key without changing the original parameter object? Explain removal of an absent key, what bracket lookup versus get_list returns, whether editing the returned list mutates the parameters, and what happens if the caller instead tries item assignment or update in place.

criteria.description: add returns a new QueryParams with the existing values followed by the appended value; set returns a new QueryParams replacing the entire value list with one value. Both copy the key mapping and replace the affected list instead of modifying the original parameter object.

remove creates a new parameter object with a copied mapping and removes the whole key, including every value. Its pop with a default makes removal of an absent key a no-op on the resulting values, without changing the original.

Bracket lookup returns the first stored value for the key, whereas get_list returns all values in a newly constructed list (or an empty list for an absent key). Mutating that returned list therefore cannot mutate the stored parameter values.
In-place item assignment and update both explicitly raise RuntimeError because QueryParams are immutable, directing callers to copy-returning set or merge rather than altering the existing object.

material_error_examples: add replaces all existing values instead of appending one.
set modifies the original parameter object in place.
Removing an absent key raises KeyError.
get_list exposes the internal mutable value list.
Item assignment is supported as an in-place equivalent of set.

questions.question: When decoding response text, how does HTTPX choose between an explicitly assigned encoding, the Content-Type charset, and default_encoding? Describe handling of an unrecognized header charset when the body is already buffered, when a callable default is invoked, and what happens if encoding is first inspected before an unbuffered body is read with no charset header and a callable default. Also explain text caching and whether encoding can be reassigned after text has been accessed.

criteria.description: Explicit assignment stores the encoding used by later access; otherwise the header charset is considered first and checked as a known codec. With buffered content, an absent or unrecognized header charset falls back to a string default or the callable default, with a falsey result falling back to UTF-8.
The callable default receives the complete stored _content bytes, and is only invoked if those bytes already exist when encoding is first determined.

With no charset header and no buffered content, initial encoding access cannot call the detector and caches UTF-8; merely reading the body later does not recompute that cached encoding or trigger detection.

text lazily caches its result, including an empty string for empty content, and uses the chosen encoding for nonempty content. Once _text exists the encoding setter raises ValueError rather than invalidating/redecoding the cached text.

material_error_examples: A callable default_encoding runs separately for every streamed text chunk.
Reading the body automatically reruns charset detection even if encoding was already cached.
Assigning encoding after reading text invalidates the text cache and decodes it again.
An unrecognized charset header necessarily wins over a configured string default.

questions.question: When the default HTTP transports encounter a lower-level httpcore failure, how is the public HTTPX exception chosen if both a broad class and a subclass match? Explain what happens to an unmatched exception, how the message and original cause are preserved, and whether conversion covers failures while initially obtaining a response and while later consuming its body in both synchronous and asynchronous use.

criteria.description: The mapping includes broad and specific httpcore exception classes, and scans all isinstance matches, replacing a current target with a subclass target; this selects e.g. HTTPX ReadTimeout rather than only TimeoutException.
If no mapped class matches, the original exception is re-raised unchanged.
For a match, a new mapped exception is constructed with str(original) as its message and raised from the original exception, preserving explicit cause chaining.

Both transport request handlers wrap their pool request call in the conversion context and return wrapped response streams; both synchronous and asynchronous response-stream iteration also run inside that context, covering later body-iteration failures.

material_error_examples: The first matching broad exception class always wins over a specific subclass.
An unmatched exception is converted into a generic HTTPError.
Exception translation only covers obtaining response headers, not subsequent body iteration.
The mapped exception drops the original exception cause.

questions.question: How does URLPattern determine which mounted transport a synchronous HTTPX client uses for a URL? Explain the scheme and port constraints, the differences between example.com, *.example.com, and *example.com host patterns, the precedence when several mounts match, and what happens when the winning mount is None or no mount matches.

criteria.description: An all:// pattern has no scheme constraint; other nonempty schemes must equal the URL scheme. A non-None normalized parsed pattern port must equal the URL port. Scheme-default ports normalize to None, so an explicit :443 in an https pattern adds no port constraint and can match that host on another HTTPS port.

An exact host matches only itself; *.example.com matches subdomains but not the apex, while *example.com matches both the apex and dot-separated subdomains, not arbitrary suffix matches. Empty or * hosts impose no hostname regex.

Client mounts are converted to URLPattern keys and sorted; priority is lexicographic with a non-None normalized parsed port first, then longer host, then longer scheme, and selection stops at the first matching pattern. An explicit scheme-default port, such as :443 for https, normalizes to None and supplies no port-priority advantage.
A first matching mount whose transport is None selects the main transport immediately rather than continuing to broader mounts; no matching mount also selects the main transport.

material_error_examples: *.example.com also matches the bare example.com host.
Mounts are always tried in insertion order, regardless of specificity.
A matching None mount is skipped so that the next matching proxy transport can be used.
An explicitly written :443 on an https mount both restricts it to port 443 and gives it port-specific priority.

questions.question: Why does the default filter preserve an ordinary false value unless its boolean option is enabled, yet accept even a StrictUndefined value without truth-testing it? Also explain why missing.child['leaf']|default('fallback') can reach the fallback with ChainableUndefined but fail with ordinary Undefined, and whether ChainableUndefined also makes arithmetic on a missing value safe before the filter runs.

criteria.description: The filter returns the supplied default for any Undefined instance, or for a false value only when boolean is true; otherwise it returns the original value, so defined false values are preserved by the normal mode.

The isinstance(value, Undefined) condition is evaluated first and short-circuits the boolean test. StrictUndefined inherits Undefined and its __bool__ raises through _fail_with_undefined_error, but that method is not invoked when default sees the undefined value itself, even with boolean enabled.

Ordinary Undefined fails on normal attribute access and item lookup, before the filter can receive the nested expression result. ChainableUndefined instead returns itself from normal attribute and item access, preserving an Undefined instance all the way to default.

Chainability does not make arithmetic safe: ChainableUndefined inherits the failing arithmetic operations from Undefined, so adding to a missing value raises the undefined exception before a fallback filter can act; the filter is a value check, not an exception handler.

material_error_examples: The default filter always replaces False, zero, and empty strings.
With boolean enabled, default truth-tests StrictUndefined before deciding whether to use the fallback.
Ordinary Undefined supports arbitrary nested missing lookups until the final filter.
ChainableUndefined makes arithmetic on missing values safe, or default catches errors raised while evaluating its input.

template candidate selection and missing-template fallback
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Fallback-filter type checking and short-circuiting interact with undefined subclass operations; this asks about post-resolution missing-value behavior, not Environment.getitem/getattr resolution order or loader fallback.

questions.question: When a template serializes a value with the tojson filter, how are the serializer and its keyword arguments selected by default and by policy overrides? Explain how a per-call indent interacts with those policy arguments, which extra HTML-safety transformations and result type are applied, and why the result still needs care inside a double-quoted HTML attribute.

criteria.description: The filter obtains json.dumps_function and json.dumps_kwargs from the evaluation environment policies; defaults are a None function and sort_keys=True, and the helper substitutes json.dumps when the configured function is None, otherwise calling the configured serializer with the policy kwargs.

When indent is not None, the filter copies the kwargs mapping and replaces its indent entry for this call; it does not mutate the policy mapping. With no per-call indent it passes the policy kwargs through unchanged.
After serialization the helper replaces less-than, greater-than, ampersand, and apostrophe with their Unicode escapes and wraps the output in Markup so it is treated as HTML-safe.

The HTML-safety transformations do not make JSON safe directly in a double-quoted HTML attribute because double quotes are not escaped by those replacements. Naming alternative quoting or escaping techniques is optional.

material_error_examples: Supplying indent mutates the environment policy dictionary for later calls.
The default serializer is hard-coded and cannot be replaced by policies.
The helper HTML-escapes all quote characters, so its Markup is safe unchanged inside double-quoted attributes.
The result is an ordinary unmarked string.

questions.question: For a synchronous LoopContext wrapping a generator, how do last and nextitem share lookahead without skipping an item on the next iteration? Explain how requesting length after iteration and lookahead have already begun computes and preserves the total, how advancing updates the current/previous item and index, and what last and nextitem report at exhaustion.

criteria.description: last and nextitem both call _peek_next, which returns the cached _after item or advances the underlying iterator once and caches it; repeated peeks at an available next item do not consume more items.

length caches its result; when len on the original iterable raises TypeError, it materializes the remaining iterator, replaces that iterator for continued traversal, and adds the number already consumed (index) plus any cached lookahead item to the remaining count.
Advancing consumes and clears _after if present, otherwise reads the underlying iterator, then increments index0, moves _current into _before, and sets _current to the next item.
At exhaustion the missing sentinel makes last true; nextitem constructs the configured undefined value rather than returning None or raising StopIteration itself.

material_error_examples: Each access to last or nextitem consumes another generator item even if a next item is already cached.
Computing length after iteration starts reports only the unconsumed tail or discards that tail.
nextitem returns None at exhaustion.

template candidate selection and missing-template fallback
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Synchronous loop metadata maintains lookahead and iteration state, including length recovery for unsized iterables; this is runtime iteration, not parsing, compilation, loading, caching, or environment lookup precedence.

questions.question: How does native_concat determine the result type of a synchronous NativeTemplate.render call? Trace how rendered outputs reach it, distinguish empty output, a single non-string value, a single string, and multiple outputs, and explain literal parsing, leading-whitespace handling, and which parsing failures leave the result as text.

criteria.description: NativeEnvironment uses native_concat as concat, and NativeTemplate.render creates a context and passes root_render_func(ctx) to its environment class concat function.
native_concat samples up to two outputs: no outputs returns None, while exactly one non-string output is returned unchanged; a single string continues to literal parsing.
Multiple outputs are converted with str and joined without a separator; when the source is a generator the sampled head is chained back before the remaining outputs so it is not lost.

The resulting string is parsed with ast.parse in eval mode before literal_eval, preserving leading spaces/tabs instead of letting literal_eval strip them; successful literal evaluation returns the native value, while ValueError, SyntaxError, or MemoryError returns the unparsed string.

material_error_examples: Native rendering always returns a string.
An empty rendered output sequence becomes an empty string.
A single non-string result is stringified and parsed again.
All exceptions during literal parsing are swallowed, or leading whitespace is deliberately stripped first.

excluded_topics_avoided: filesystem template loading and uptodate checks
atomic filesystem bytecode-cache writes and cleanup
template candidate selection and missing-template fallback
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Result aggregation and Python-literal recovery in the native rendering caller and helper, not the previously excluded source-to-code compilation pipeline.

questions.question: When streaming a template, what changes when output buffering is enabled, and what does the buffer size actually count? Explain the initial and disabled modes, how empty chunks and an incomplete final batch are handled (including an all-empty remainder), whether disabling restarts generation, and what happens for a size of one or less.

criteria.description: Template.stream wraps generate in TemplateStream, which initially disables buffering. Disabled iteration delegates directly to the existing generator, so disabling buffering resumes that generator rather than restarting rendering.

Enabling installs a buffered generator. That generator appends every chunk but increments its size counter only for truthy/nonempty chunks, so the limit counts nonempty output chunks rather than characters, bytes, or every yielded chunk.

A completed batch is concatenated and its buffer/counter reset. On exhaustion a batch containing at least one nonempty chunk is emitted even below the requested size; an empty or all-empty remainder ends without yielding an empty batch.
A requested buffer size of one or less raises ValueError before enabling the new buffering mode; the exact diagnostic wording is not required.

material_error_examples: The buffer size counts characters or bytes.
Empty chunks count toward the batch limit and an all-empty remainder yields a final empty string.
Disabling buffering starts the template over from its first output.
A size of one silently switches to unbuffered mode.

excluded_topics_avoided: filesystem template loading and uptodate checks
atomic filesystem bytecode-cache writes and cleanup
template candidate selection and missing-template fallback
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Streaming output batching, chunk accounting, and iteration-mode changes; no loader selection or template/bytecode-cache mechanism is involved.

questions.question: For CPython wheel-tag generation, what determines whether the automatically generated stable-ABI family is abi3 or abi3t? Explain how an explicit ABI list determines free-threaded status, the version eligibility rule and lower-version reach of stable tags, where those tags appear relative to native and none tags, and how behavior changes when only a major Python version is supplied.

criteria.description: Free-threaded status is determined from the first ABI only: it must match a cp-plus-digits prefix and have t in the remaining ABI flags; an empty or nonmatching first ABI is not threaded. This detection happens before the specially handled ABI names are removed from the explicit list.

Automatic abi3 requires a major/minor version at least 3.2 and a non-threaded ABI; automatic abi3t uses the same version threshold but requires threading. Thus abi3t generation is not gated at 3.15. The chosen stable ABI is also generated for earlier minors down through 3.2, not 3.1.

After the specially handled ABI entries are removed, native/remaining explicit ABI tags are emitted first, followed by current-interpreter stable ABI tags, then current-interpreter none tags, and finally descending older-minor stable tags. Within-family ABI/platform loop order is optional supporting detail, not required for credit.

For a major-only Python version the default ABI list is empty and both stable-ABI eligibility checks fail, so there is no automatic stable ABI or older-minor ladder. Any remaining user-supplied ABI entries can still yield tags, followed by none tags.

material_error_examples: The presence of t in any ABI entry makes the whole ABI list free-threaded.
abi3t tags are automatically generated only for Python 3.15 and newer.
Free-threaded builds automatically receive both abi3 and abi3t stable families.
The backward stable-ABI ladder includes Python 3.1.
A major-only version automatically discovers the host interpreter native ABI.

excluded_topics_avoided: Version construction and parse entry point
Wheel and sdist filename structural parsing
novelty.distinct_mechanism: CPython native/stable ABI compatibility eligibility and ordering, not Version parsing or compressed tag-string expansion; independent from musl platform detection and wheel selection ranking.

questions.question: When distribution metadata is read from email-style headers and a body, how does parsing separate usable values from unparsed data instead of silently choosing a value? Cover repeated singleton or unknown headers, invalid UTF-8 header bytes, Project-URL entries with repeated labels or no comma, and Description supplied by both a header and body or by an invalid body payload.

criteria.description: Header names are made lowercase and all occurrences are retrieved. Unknown fields retain their complete value list in unparsed; ordinary singleton string fields are unwrapped only for one value, with repeated singleton values going to unparsed instead of first/last-wins.

Byte-derived Header chunks are checked with strict UTF-8; invalid chunks use Latin-1 to preserve a string representation and mark the entire header field invalid, placing all its values in unparsed instead of raw.

Project-URL parsing partitions on the first comma and strips both sides; no comma produces an empty URL. A repeated exact label raises KeyError and causes the entire field value list to go to unparsed, rather than overwriting a mapping entry.

A successfully decoded nonempty body becomes raw description only when no description header data exists; with an accepted raw header, that header is removed from raw and both values are placed in unparsed, while an already-unparsed header list gains the decoded body. String input requires a string payload, and byte input requires bytes decodable as strict UTF-8. Invalid or multipart payloads raise internally and the parser appends its fallback payload to unparsed description without removing an accepted raw Description header; that fallback may be None for byte-input multipart messages.

material_error_examples: Repeated Name headers silently keep the final value.
A malformed UTF-8 header is decoded with replacement and accepted into raw metadata.
Repeated Project-URL labels overwrite earlier URLs.
The message body always takes precedence over the Description header.
A Project-URL entry without a comma immediately raises out of the parser.

excluded_topics_avoided: Version construction and parse entry point
Wheel and sdist filename structural parsing
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Lenient metadata ingestion with field quarantine, compound-header conversion, and description conflicts; none of the excluded mechanisms covers email metadata parsing.

questions.question: How does canonicalize_license_expression validate and normalize an SPDX expression? Assume any LicenseRef suffixes in the expression are distinct under case-insensitive comparison. Explain how it rejects malformed boolean/parenthesis syntax, where WITH is allowed and how its operand is checked, how ordinary license identifiers and a trailing + are normalized, and how LicenseRef spelling and allowed suffix characters differ from ordinary licenses.

criteria.description: Empty input is rejected; parentheses are padded for whitespace tokenization and tokens are lowercased. A placeholder Python expression is compiled to check syntax, with explicit checks rejecting an opening parenthesis after an operand and empty parentheses; syntax failures become InvalidLicenseExpression.

WITH must immediately follow a license operand and precede a non-operator/non-parenthesis token; it cannot follow an already processed exception or a closing parenthesis. Its operand must be in EXCEPTIONS and is emitted using the canonical exception ID; invalid placement or unknown exceptions raise InvalidLicenseExpression.

Ordinary licenses are looked up case-insensitively in LICENSES after removing an optional trailing +; unknown identifiers raise InvalidLicenseExpression, and known ones use the canonical ID with + restored. Operators are uppercase and final spacing removes spaces just inside parentheses.

Under the question's distinct-suffix premise, LicenseRef lookup uses a lowercased key but reconstructs the LicenseRef- prefix with the original suffix spelling. The lowercased suffix must match [A-Za-z0-9.-]+, so it must be nonempty and contain only ASCII letters, digits, dots, or hyphens after lowercasing; this does not impose an ASCII-only restriction on the original spelling. A trailing + is rejected rather than normalized.

material_error_examples: WITH may be applied to an entire parenthesized expression.
LicenseRef suffixes are always lowercased and may contain underscores.
A + suffix is accepted for LicenseRef identifiers exactly as for SPDX license IDs.
Unknown exception names are accepted if they are known license names.

excluded_topics_avoided: Version construction and parse entry point
Wheel and sdist filename structural parsing
novelty.distinct_mechanism: SPDX expression grammar, exception attachment, and identifier validation; not project-name canonicalization or requirement tokenization.

questions.question: How does Linux platform-tag generation decide whether musllinux compatibility applies to the running Python rather than merely to the host OS? Explain discovery of the loader and cases that produce no musllinux tags, how its version output is interpreted, the architecture/version ordering of generated tags, and how these tags fit after Linux architecture adjustment and other Linux platform tags.

criteria.description: Detection opens sys.executable as ELF and gets the interpreter from its PT_INTERP program header, not an OS distribution label. ELF interpreter lookup skips non-PT_INTERP headers and headers whose unpacking raises struct.error, such as truncated headers, and returns a NUL-stripped loader path, or None. Seek/read OSError is not skipped per header: it aborts detection for the executable. Opening/parsing OSError, TypeError, or ValueError and missing/non-musl loader paths make musl detection return None.

The loader is run directly with check=False and stderr captured as text. Blank output lines are discarded and whitespace stripped; the first nonblank line must begin with musl and the second must match Version followed by major.minor. Missing or unrecognized output returns None; a patch component is not part of the stored version.

Without a detected musl version the generator yields nothing. Otherwise it processes architectures in input order and, for each, emits musllinux tags from the detected minor down through zero while keeping the detected major and architecture fixed.

Linux integration rewrites x86_64 to i686 and aarch64 to armv8l for a 32-bit interpreter, expands armv8l into armv8l then armv7l, emits all plain linux architecture tags first, then manylinux tags, then musllinux tags using the same architecture list.

material_error_examples: The mere presence of musl on the host makes every Python executable musllinux-compatible.
The musl version is read from the loader stdout.
Older musl major versions are enumerated as well as older minor versions.
musllinux tags precede plain linux tags in the Linux platform generator.
On a 32-bit interpreter an aarch64 platform remains aarch64.

excluded_topics_avoided: Version construction and parse entry point
Wheel and sdist filename structural parsing
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Executable-linked libc detection and Linux compatibility-tag generation; distinct from parsing or expanding an existing compressed platform-tag string.

questions.question: In Pylock.select, assume a valid lock and packages that have already passed environment and package checks. How is each installation source chosen? Explain direct-source handling and when prefer_sdist_predicate is called, how supplied supported-tag order ranks compatible wheels (including repeated tags and tied wheels), and when selection falls back to an sdist or raises an error.

criteria.description: A package with VCS, directory, or archive source yields that source directly. Otherwise, an available sdist is chosen before wheel matching only when the supplied predicate returns true for the package name; the predicate is not called when the sdist is absent or a direct-source branch was taken.

Supported tags receive ascending preference ranks, retaining the first occurrence of duplicates; incompatible wheels are discarded and a compatible wheel is ranked by its best matching tag. Optional supporting detail, not required for credit: explicitly supplied tags, even an empty sequence, are used unchanged; omitted tags use sys_tags.

Compatible candidates are stably sorted by best-tag rank, so equally ranked wheels retain their order in the package wheels sequence. Selection takes only the first resulting wheel and yields it with its package.

If wheels exist but none matches, an available sdist is used; otherwise PylockSelectError is raised for lack of a compatible wheel and an sdist fallback. With no wheels but an sdist, that sdist is yielded even without source preference. Optional supporting detail, not required for credit: the diagnostic identifies the package and its index.

material_error_examples: The predicate is called for every package, even when no sdist exists.
The first wheel listed wins even if a later wheel has a more preferred supported tag.
Repeated supported tags replace the rank recorded for their first occurrence.
An explicitly empty tags sequence is replaced by sys_tags.
An incompatible wheel is used when no sdist is available.

excluded_topics_avoided: Version construction and parse entry point
Wheel and sdist filename structural parsing
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Install-artifact choice, stable supported-tag ranking, and source fallback after eligibility checks; not filename parsing, compressed tag expansion, marker environment merging, or version-constraint filtering.

questions.question: When specifications are added after implementations already exist, how do whole-hook and argument-specific deprecation warnings differ? Explain which signature parameters select argument warnings, including defaulted and keyword-only parameters, the order relative to unknown required-argument validation, and whose source location and warning category are used. Assume nonhistoric hooks and warning filters that allow warning emission.

criteria.description: Adding specifications to existing callers verifies their current implementations. A configured whole-hook warning is emitted for the implementation without selecting a particular argument.

Argument warnings are selected by iterating HookImpl.argnames and looking up each name in warn_on_impl_args; non-None mapped warnings are emitted. HookImpl obtains argnames from varnames, which omits keyword-only parameters and separates defaulted positional parameters into kwargnames, so those parameters do not select argument warnings.

Whole-hook warning emission precedes the unknown-required-argument check, while argument-specific warning emission follows it. Thus a required-argument mismatch can emit the whole-hook warning and then raise PluginValidationError before any argument warnings are emitted.

Warnings use warn_explicit with the supplied warning instance and its concrete type, and the implementation function's code filename and first line number, rather than the specification's source location or the caller's stack location.

material_error_examples: Argument deprecation warnings are selected from all supplied call keyword arguments.
Defaulted and keyword-only implementation parameters select warnings just like required positional parameters.
Warnings are attributed to the hookspec function's declaration.
An unknown required argument is rejected before any whole-hook warning can be emitted.

novelty.distinct_mechanism: Deprecation-warning selection, validation precedence, and source attribution during late specification verification. Adjacent to registration validation, but the question does not trace registration or marker-option discovery; it also differs from runtime monitoring exceptions.

questions.question: An existing hook caller has implementations but no specification. Once a matching specification is recognized during a later specification addition, how is it attached, and what happens if an existing implementation declares a required positional parameter absent from the specification's required positional parameters? Explain whether the failed addition leaves the caller unspecified, whether retrying with a corrected specification can replace it, and what happens when a supplied namespace contains no matching specifications.

criteria.description: For the existing caller, the manager attaches the recognized specification before verifying the caller's existing implementations.

Validation compares the implementation's required positional parameter names to the specification's required positional parameter names. Any implementation-only names raise PluginValidationError identifying the mismatched names.

The specification is assigned before existing implementations are checked, without rollback on a validation failure. The caller therefore remains specified, and a later attempt to set even a corrected specification raises ValueError because replacement is disallowed.
If no matching specifications are found, add_hookspecs raises ValueError instead of treating the namespace as a successful no-op.

material_error_examples: Existing implementations are validated before the specification is attached, making a failed addition atomic.
A corrected specification silently replaces the specification left by a failed addition.
A namespace containing no matching specifications is accepted as an empty no-op.

novelty.distinct_mechanism: Late specification attachment and non-atomic failure state, starting from a recognized specification rather than marker discovery. Adjacent to registration validation, but the question starts with existing implementations and does not ask how plugins are registered or ordered.

questions.question: A plugin exposes a required public hook, an optional public hook, and an underscore-prefixed hook, none with a specification. When the manager performs its explicit pending-hook validation, which of these can fail and why? Explain what changes if a caller already has a specification, what error identifies an offending implementation, and whether the check removes or changes implementations as it runs.

criteria.description: Pending validation examines only relay names that do not start with an underscore and only callers whose spec is None; callers already carrying a specification are skipped rather than revalidated.

For an examined unknown public hook it checks each implementation's optionalhook flag. An optional implementation is permitted, but a nonoptional implementation raises PluginValidationError; the underscore-prefixed hook is outside this check.
The raised PluginValidationError names the unknown hook and offending plugin. The check only reads state; it neither removes implementations nor changes their optional status.

material_error_examples: Unknown hooks fail pending validation even when every implementation is marked optionalhook.
Underscore-prefixed hooks undergo the same pending validation as public hooks.
Pending validation removes offending implementations before raising.
Pending validation repeats signature checking for every specified hook.

novelty.distinct_mechanism: Explicit post-discovery enforcement for still-unknown public hooks and optionalhook exemptions. Adjacent to plugin registration, but not registration orchestration or blocked-name removal; no late-spec attachment behavior is required here.

questions.question: For TagTracer, how do nested subtracers build their tags and how does processor selection treat a colon-separated registration versus a parent-tag registration? Explain how an installed writer renders ordinary arguments and a trailing dictionary at a nonzero indent, whether processors receive that rendered form or the original arguments, and what happens for an emission with no arguments or with no writer.

criteria.description: A root get creates a one-element tag tuple, and each subtracer get appends a tag while retaining the root. A string processor registration is split on colons; processor lookup is for the exact tuple, not its parent prefixes.

The writer joins ordinary arguments with spaces, prefixes two spaces per indent level, and appends the colon-joined tags in brackets and a newline. A trailing dictionary is removed from that content and rendered as indented key/value lines with four additional spaces.
The writer receives the formatted string, while a matching processor receives the original tag tuple and original argument tuple, including any trailing dictionary.
No arguments suppress writer invocation but do not suppress processor lookup or invocation; no writer likewise does not disable processors. Missing exact-tag processors are ignored.

material_error_examples: A processor registered for a parent tag automatically receives all descendant emissions.
Processors receive the writer's rendered text with the trailing dictionary removed.
An empty emission is ignored by both writer and processor.

novelty.distinct_mechanism: Low-level tag-channel routing and message rendering, independent of PluginManager hook-call monitoring, Result capture, or monitoring undo.

questions.question: How does varnames turn a class, callable instance, or bound method into its pair of parameter-name tuples? Explain which parameter kinds are retained, how defaults divide the tuples, how implicit receiver names are removed, and which introspection failures produce empty tuples rather than propagating.

criteria.description: Classes are inspected through __init__; non-routine callable objects are resolved through __call__; bound methods are inspected through __func__. Missing class __init__ and an Exception-derived failure looking up a callable object's __call__ return two empty tuples.

Only positional-only and positional-or-keyword parameters are retained; variadic and keyword-only parameters are omitted. The trailing retained parameters with defaults form the second tuple; the first tuple contains the remaining retained names.

The first required name is removed for a bound method, or for a qualified callable whose first required name is self (also obj on PyPy). This stripping applies to args, not the tuple of defaulted names.
TypeError from inspect.signature returns two empty tuples; the code does not generally swallow other signature-inspection exceptions such as ValueError.

material_error_examples: Keyword-only parameters are placed in the second tuple.
Every exception from inspect.signature is caught and converted to empty tuples.
A parameter named self is always removed, even from an unqualified ordinary function.

novelty.distinct_mechanism: Signature normalization and partitioning before HookImpl/HookSpec metadata exists, rather than marker parsing, registration orchestration, or argument dispatch during multicall.

questions.question: A session has its default adapters plus custom adapters mounted for "https://api.example.test" and "https://api.example.test/v1/". How does sending a prepared request choose between them, including URL case differences and registration order? Explain whether the shorter host-looking prefix is restricted to that exact host, what remounting an identical prefix does, and what happens when no registered prefix matches.

criteria.description: Session.send selects an adapter using the prepared request URL; mount orders registrations by descending prefix length, and get_adapter returns the first match, so the /v1/ registration wins for matching URLs regardless of which of these differently sized prefixes was mounted first.

Matching lowercases both the complete URL and registered prefix and uses startswith, not parsed hostname equality or a host-boundary test. Therefore the host-looking prefix also matches a URL beginning https://api.example.test.attacker.invalid unless a higher-priority prefix matches.
Mounting the identical prefix assigns a replacement adapter at that mapping key, rather than accumulating another registration; it then moves only shorter prefixes behind it.
If no prefix matches, get_adapter raises InvalidSchema with a message that no connection adapters were found for the URL; it does not select an arbitrary default adapter.

material_error_examples: The most recently mounted adapter always wins, even when its prefix is shorter.
Adapter selection compares parsed hostnames, so a host-looking prefix cannot match a longer hostname.
Adapter prefix matching is case-sensitive.
An unmatched URL silently uses the default HTTPS adapter.

excluded_topics_avoided: Adapter response construction over a pooled connection
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Adapter registry ordering and literal URL-prefix dispatch decide which transport is selected before sending; no pooling/response conversion, certificate configuration, environment merge, or top-level helper call chain is requested.

questions.question: When PreparedRequest.copy invokes _copy_cookie_jar, what happens for no jar, a jar exposing copy(), and a generic CookieJar without copy()? For a RequestsCookieJar, explain whether the returned jar, its cookie objects, and its policy are shared with the original, including the depth of copying. Would assigning a different value attribute to a copied cookie or mutating the policy through the copied jar affect the original?

criteria.description: PreparedRequest.copy delegates its cookie jar to _copy_cookie_jar; None stays None, and any jar exposing copy is delegated to that method rather than being checked by an explicit RequestsCookieJar type test.
RequestsCookieJar.copy creates a new RequestsCookieJar but installs the same policy instance returned by get_policy, so mutation of that shared policy is visible through both jars.

RequestsCookieJar.copy populates the new jar through update; updating from a CookieJar inserts copy.copy(cookie) for each cookie. Cookie objects are distinct shallow copies, so assigning a copied cookie value does not change the original cookie value, but this is not a recursive deep copy of cookie internals.
Without a copy method, the helper shallow-copies the generic jar, clears the new jar, and repopulates it with shallow copies of each original cookie before returning it.

material_error_examples: Copying a RequestsCookieJar deep-copies its CookiePolicy.
The copied jar stores the original Cookie objects, so assigning a copied cookie value also changes the original.
A jar with no copy method is returned unchanged.
_copy_cookie_jar delegates to copy only after an isinstance check for RequestsCookieJar.

excluded_topics_avoided: Cookie name collisions, domain/path lookup, and empty-string lookup behavior
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Object ownership and shallow-copy isolation of cookie containers, cookies, and policies are independent of cookie lookup ambiguity; the request-copy caller supplies context without asking how outgoing bodies or headers are assembled.

questions.question: When can a URL be excluded from environment proxies by a no-proxy rule? Explain explicit no_proxy versus lowercase and uppercase environment variables, hostname-less URLs, and how comma-separated rules match IPv4 addresses/subnets versus hostnames with optional ports. Include subnet-prefix validity, what happens when no rule matches, how native bypass-check errors and temporarily changed environment values are handled, and what environment-proxy lookup returns for a bypassed URL.

criteria.description: An explicit no_proxy value is used instead of reading environment rules; only None falls back to a nonempty lowercase no_proxy or then uppercase NO_PROXY. URLs with no hostname immediately bypass proxies.

Rule parsing removes spaces, splits on commas, and drops empty entries. IPv4 hosts match either an exact literal address or a valid IPv4 CIDR containing the address; CIDR validation requires exactly one slash, an integer prefix from 1 through 32, and an address accepted by inet_aton. Membership compares masked host and network addresses.

For non-IPv4 hosts the code checks suffix matches against both hostname and hostname plus an explicit truthy port. This is endswith matching rather than exact hostname equality or a label-boundary check, and it does not use the IPv4 subnet path.

If local matching does not bypass, proxy_bypass is called with the parsed hostname under a temporary lowercase no_proxy set to the original explicit argument. None does not alter the environment; otherwise the previous value is restored, or the key is removed if originally absent, in finally. TypeError and socket.gaierror from proxy_bypass are treated as no bypass; its truthy result yields True and otherwise the function returns False.
get_environ_proxies returns an empty dictionary when should_bypass_proxies succeeds; otherwise it returns getproxies(), rather than returning a no-proxy rule list as the proxy mapping.

material_error_examples: IPv4 CIDR rules accept /0 and /33 as valid prefix lengths.
Hostname rules require exact equality and cannot match a suffix without a DNS-label boundary.
The native bypass checker receives the complete URL including its port.
A supplied no_proxy argument permanently replaces the lowercase environment variable.
A bypassed URL still receives the environment proxy mapping from getproxies().

excluded_topics_avoided: Requests environment proxy/TLS settings merge precedence
AnyIO TCP Happy Eyeballs address racing
novelty.distinct_mechanism: The central mechanism is deciding address-level proxy exemption: IPv4 subnet masking, hostname/port suffix rules, and temporary platform bypass evaluation. Prior Requests environment precedence only covered merging proxy dictionaries and TLS settings, not bypass-rule matching or its native fallback.

questions.question: For a non-redirecting response, how do session response hooks transform what the caller receives? Explain when they run relative to adapter sending, elapsed-time recording, cookie persistence, and non-streamed body consumption; how one callable versus a sequence is invoked and which send options are forwarded; and how return values (including None and a falsey replacement Response) or a raised exception affect subsequent hooks and the final response. If a hook returns a response with history, which responses contribute cookies?

criteria.description: Session.send calls hooks after adapter.send and assigning elapsed, but before cookie persistence and its final non-streamed content access; it assigns the dispatch result back to r, so the replacement response proceeds through the rest of this non-redirecting send and is returned.

The dispatcher wraps a single callable in a list or iterates the supplied hook sequence in order, passing the current response and send kwargs. Session.send has supplied missing stream/verify/cert/proxy settings and removed allow_redirects from those kwargs before dispatch.

Only a None return preserves the current response; any non-None result, including a falsey Response, replaces the response passed to subsequent hooks and ultimately returned by dispatch. In-place mutation remains visible when a hook returns None.

Hook exceptions are not caught by dispatch_hook or the surrounding Session.send call, so they propagate, abort remaining hooks, and prevent reaching the later cookie-persistence and final body-consumption steps.

After hooks, session cookie persistence extracts cookies from each response in the returned response history, then from the current replacement response. The distinct request objects used as extraction context are optional supporting details.

material_error_examples: Returning None deletes the response passed to later hooks.
A falsey Response return is ignored because hook replacement checks truthiness.
Hook exceptions are swallowed and the remaining hooks still execute.
Response hooks run only after cookies and the non-streamed response body have been consumed.
Cookies from history created by hooks are ignored.

excluded_topics_avoided: Response chunk iteration and Unicode stream decoding
novelty.distinct_mechanism: The subject is ordered callback transformation, return-value/exception semantics, and post-hook consumption of the replacement response; it does not ask how redirects, streamed chunks, cookie name resolution, or environment setting precedence work.

questions.question: How does requote_uri normalize a URI containing percent-encoded unreserved characters such as %7E, encoded reserved characters such as %2F, and literal spaces? Explain what is decoded or kept escaped, which URI punctuation survives quoting, and how malformed escapes change the process. In particular, contrast a two-alphanumeric non-hex escape such as %ZZ with a lone trailing percent sign, and explain whether an invalid escape changes the handling of valid escapes elsewhere in the same URI.

criteria.description: unquote_unreserved decodes valid percent escapes only when the decoded character belongs to the ASCII letters, digits, or -._~ unreserved set. Thus %7E becomes ~, whereas %2F remains escaped because slash is not in that set.

The normal path quotes the selectively unquoted URI with percent and the listed URI punctuation marked safe, preserving existing reserved-character escapes and syntax characters such as /, ?, &, =, and # while quoting literal spaces.

The helper attempts hexadecimal conversion only for a two-character alphanumeric candidate; conversion failure such as %ZZ raises InvalidURL. A lone trailing percent has no such candidate, is reconstructed unchanged by the helper, and stays literal because percent is safe on the normal quoting path.

requote_uri catches that InvalidURL and quotes the original, not the partially unquoted URI, using a safe set without percent. Every percent in the original is then escaped, including those in otherwise valid escapes, so mixed input %7E%ZZ becomes %257E%25ZZ rather than ~%25ZZ.

material_error_examples: requote_uri decodes reserved escapes such as %2F into literal delimiters.
Any malformed percent sequence, including a lone trailing percent, triggers the fallback.
A %ZZ escape is propagated to the caller as InvalidURL by requote_uri.
Fallback repairs only the invalid escape and preserves other valid percent escapes unchanged.

novelty.distinct_mechanism: Selective percent-unquoting and whole-original-URI fallback quoting determine how encoded delimiters and malformed escape sequences survive normalization. This is neither HTTP request assembly, redirect following, nor URL credential redaction.

questions.question: How does Config resolve and cast a setting when an environment mapping, an env file, and a default may all provide values? Explain how env_prefix affects lookup, what happens when no value exists, the accepted string forms and errors for boolean casting, how None and other casts are handled, and whether a value read through Environ can later be set or deleted through that wrapper. Assume any supplied cast is a named function or type with a __name__ attribute.

criteria.description: Config prefixes the requested key, searches the environment before file_values before an explicitly supplied default, applies casting to the chosen value, and raises KeyError if the prefixed key is missing without a default.
For a string cast to bool, lowercasing permits true/1 and false/0; other string values raise a configuration-specific ValueError rather than using ordinary nonempty-string truthiness.

No cast or a None value returns the value unchanged; otherwise the named cast function or type runs, and its TypeError or ValueError is converted to a ValueError naming the configuration key, value, and cast.
Environ records a key when __getitem__ accesses it and rejects subsequent set or delete operations for that recorded key with EnvironError; unread keys remain mutable through the wrapper.

material_error_examples: Env-file values override values in the supplied environment mapping.
Boolean casting treats any nonempty string, including false, as True.
A default of None is passed to the requested cast callable.
Environ permits a read key to be replaced or deleted through the wrapper.

excluded_topics_avoided: StreamingResponse chunk delivery and disconnect monitoring
Background task ordering and failure propagation
UploadFile in-memory versus threadpool operation dispatch
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Configuration-source precedence, type conversion, and environment read-locking; unrelated to application dispatch, request parsing, or excluded response mechanisms.

questions.question: How does Starlette handle a CORS preflight request without invoking the downstream application? Explain which requests qualify, how allowed origins, methods, and requested headers are checked (including wildcards and origin regexes), how allow_credentials changes the returned origin and Vary behavior when all origins are allowed, and what status/body are returned when checks pass or multiple checks fail.

criteria.description: Only HTTP requests with an Origin header and method OPTIONS plus Access-Control-Request-Method are intercepted as preflight; no-Origin/non-HTTP requests pass through and other origin-bearing HTTP requests use the downstream simple-response path.
Origins pass if all origins are allowed, the configured regex fullmatches, or the exact origin is in the allow list. A rejected origin adds an origin failure.

A wildcard in allow_methods expands to the defined method set; the requested method must be a member. Allowed header names combine safelisted and configured headers and are lowercased for checking; requested header names are split, lowercased and stripped, while allow_headers wildcard mirrors the supplied requested-header string.

Preflight installs Vary: Origin whenever origins are restricted or credentials are enabled, and echoes the requested origin in Allow-Origin only if that origin passes the origin check. With all origins allowed and credentials disabled it returns wildcard Allow-Origin instead; enabling credentials adds Allow-Credentials: true and causes a passing origin to be echoed even under wildcard origin configuration.

Failures accumulate in origin, method, headers order (at most one headers failure), yielding plaintext Disallowed CORS followed by the comma-separated failures with status 400; success returns plaintext OK with status 200. Both use the assembled preflight headers.

material_error_examples: Every OPTIONS request is intercepted even without Origin or Access-Control-Request-Method.
An origin regex only needs to match a prefix of the requesting origin.
Only the first failing CORS category is reported.
Allowing all origins always returns wildcard Allow-Origin even with credentials enabled.
A disallowed preflight request is delegated to the endpoint to determine its response.

excluded_topics_avoided: StreamingResponse chunk delivery and disconnect monitoring
Background task ordering and failure propagation
UploadFile in-memory versus threadpool operation dispatch
novelty.distinct_mechanism: CORS preflight interception, policy checks, and negotiated response headers, not generic middleware stack construction or route dispatch.

questions.question: When HTTP response compression is enabled, how does Starlette decide whether to gzip a response and when to release its response-start message? Cover request eligibility, an already-set Content-Encoding, a completed body below or at the minimum size, and a body sent with more_body=True. Explain the Content-Length, Content-Encoding, and Vary changes and how later body messages complete the compressed stream.

criteria.description: The middleware invokes its compression responder only for HTTP when Accept-Encoding contains the substring gzip; otherwise the app receives the original send. A response with any existing Content-Encoding is forwarded without recompression, releasing the saved response start on its first body.

The responder saves http.response.start rather than immediately sending it. On the first unencoded body, it bypasses compression only if the body is strictly smaller than minimum_size and more_body is false, then sends the saved start and unchanged body.

A completed first body at or above the threshold is compressed and the gzip file closed; the body becomes compressed bytes, Content-Encoding is gzip, Content-Length becomes the compressed byte length, and Vary gains Accept-Encoding before start and body are sent.

A first body with more_body true starts streaming compression regardless of its size, adds gzip Content-Encoding and Accept-Encoding to Vary, and removes Content-Length. Body messages feed the same gzip stream and forward newly buffered compressed bytes after clearing the buffer; the final message closes gzip before extracting and sending those final bytes.

material_error_examples: The minimum size threshold prevents compression of a streaming response whose first chunk is small.
Response start is forwarded before compression headers can be decided.
An existing Content-Encoding is overwritten with gzip.
Streaming compression preserves the original Content-Length.
Each body message is compressed as a separate independently closed gzip stream.

excluded_topics_avoided: StreamingResponse chunk delivery and disconnect monitoring
Background task ordering and failure propagation
UploadFile in-memory versus threadpool operation dispatch
novelty.distinct_mechanism: GZip middleware negotiation, compression thresholds and encoded-header/body transitions. It does not ask how StreamingResponse produces chunks or monitors disconnects, the excluded streaming mechanism.

questions.question: How does requires use credentials supplied by AuthenticationMiddleware to authorize HTTP and WebSocket endpoints? Explain what credentials and user are installed when the backend returns None, whether multiple required scopes are all required, and what missing scopes do for synchronous or asynchronous HTTP endpoints with and without a redirect versus WebSocket endpoints. Include the HTTP redirect target/status and whether the protected endpoint executes on denial.

criteria.description: AuthenticationMiddleware awaits the backend, replaces a None result with empty AuthCredentials and an UnauthenticatedUser, stores auth/user in the connection scope, and calls the app; the connection auth property exposes that scope value.
has_required_scope requires every required scope to appear in conn.auth.scopes, so any missing scope denies access.

For both sync and async HTTP endpoints, missing scopes cause HTTPException with the configured status (403 by default), or a 303 RedirectResponse to request.url_for(redirect) with URL-encoded next containing the original request URL; denial returns or raises without invoking the protected callable.
For a WebSocket endpoint, missing scopes await websocket.close rather than applying the HTTP status or redirect; the wrapped endpoint is awaited only when scopes pass.

material_error_examples: Possessing any one of the required scopes is sufficient.
A backend result of None prevents the application from running.
The HTTP redirect uses status 302 and discards the original request URL.
The configured HTTP redirect also redirects unauthorized WebSocket endpoints.
The protected callable runs before the decorator checks authorization.

excluded_topics_avoided: StreamingResponse chunk delivery and disconnect monitoring
Background task ordering and failure propagation
UploadFile in-memory versus threadpool operation dispatch
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Authorization scope checks and denial policy linked to backend credential population; WebSocket close is an authorization outcome, not a question about its excluded protocol state machine.

questions.question: For Starlette cookie-backed sessions, how is an incoming cookie converted into session data, and when does the outgoing HTTP response create, refresh, delete, or leave the cookie alone? Distinguish a missing or invalidly signed cookie from a successfully verified and decoded cookie, including one whose decoded session is empty, and explain whether unchanged nonempty session data is written again and whether the stored data is encrypted. Assume successfully verified cookies contain valid base64-encoded JSON session data.

criteria.description: The middleware starts with an initially-empty flag; a missing cookie or BadSignature produces an empty scope session without clearing that flag, so an untouched empty session in those cases does not generate a deletion cookie.

Incoming data is verified with TimestampSigner.unsign using max_age, then base64-decoded and JSON-loaded into scope session; successful verification and decoding set the initially-empty flag false even when the decoded data is empty. This is signing plus encoding, not encryption.
At http.response.start any truthy session is JSON-encoded, base64-encoded, signed, and appended as Set-Cookie. There is no changed-data check, so unchanged nonempty sessions are also persisted again.

If the outgoing session is empty but the incoming cookie successfully verified and decoded, response start appends a deletion Set-Cookie that expires the cookie; this also covers a valid cookie whose decoded data was already empty. Otherwise an empty session emits no session cookie.

material_error_examples: Session cookies are encrypted and cannot be decoded by clients.
A missing or bad-signature cookie always triggers a deletion Set-Cookie.
Only session mutations cause nonempty data to be written back.
A verified cookie containing an empty session is treated the same as no incoming cookie.

excluded_topics_avoided: StreamingResponse chunk delivery and disconnect monitoring
Background task ordering and failure propagation
UploadFile in-memory versus threadpool operation dispatch
novelty.distinct_mechanism: Signed client-side session restoration and response-cookie persistence/deletion, independent of lazy request parsing and all excluded response dispatch mechanisms.

questions.question: For an option configured to prompt, how do command-line values, environment values, context default-map values, and the option default affect whether prompting happens? Explain the required/prompt_required and resilient-parsing gates, the source recorded after a prompt, and how boolean confirmation differs from ordinary value prompting, including evaluation of callable defaults and input-processing settings.

criteria.description: The inherited consumer checks the command line, environment, context default map, then get_default, falling through only on None and assigning the corresponding source. Thus values supplied by the first three sources bypass the prompt gate, while a value from the option-default path remains eligible.

Prompting requires source None or DEFAULT, a non-None prompt, required or prompt_required to be true, and resilient_parsing to be false. A successful prompt replaces the value and records ParameterSource.PROMPT.

The prompt path obtains its default before interacting; get_default consults the context default map, falls back to the option default, and calls callable defaults when call is true. A boolean flag uses confirm, preserving None but coercing any non-None default to bool.

Ordinary prompting passes the type, hide_input, and confirmation_prompt settings and uses process_value as value_proc. A missing default is passed as None so an actual valid value must be entered. Display-only show_choices and show_default forwarding details are optional.

material_error_examples: A configured prompt always overrides environment and default-map values.
prompt_required=False disables prompting even for a required option.
Resilient parsing still asks interactive questions.
Prompted values retain ParameterSource.DEFAULT.
A string-valued show_default is forwarded as the default label to the ordinary input prompt.

novelty.distinct_mechanism: Runtime value-source precedence and interactive prompt gating, not constructing Click parameters from annotations or adapting user callback signatures.

questions.question: How does get_typer_from_module choose what to run from an imported module? Explain precedence and failures for explicit app/function selectors, the preference among conventional names and other objects when no selector is supplied, how a selected callable becomes runnable, and what happens if nothing qualifies.

criteria.description: An explicit app selector is checked first, even if a function selector is also present; it must resolve to a Typer instance or print a stderr error and exit with status 1. With no app selector, an explicit function selector must be callable or print a stderr error and raise typer.Exit(1).

Automatic selection first tries Typer objects named app, cli, main in that order, then any other Typer object; all those app candidates precede callable fallback. The other-name scan uses a set difference, so it does not promise a stable preference among multiple nonconventional names.

Callable fallback tries main, cli, app in that order and then other names; selected callables, including explicitly selected functions, are registered as commands on a fresh Typer instance. If no Typer object or callable qualifies, the function returns None.

material_error_examples: An explicit function selector takes precedence over an explicit app selector.
Automatic discovery runs a conventionally named function before considering a nonconventionally named Typer instance.
Fallback selection considers only Python function objects rather than any callable.
Failure to find any candidate always raises an import error instead of returning None.

novelty.distinct_mechanism: Imported-module object discovery and selector failure semantics, not building the underlying command tree or recording command callbacks.

questions.question: In Rich help output, how are hidden entries and missing or empty panel names handled for arguments, options, and subcommands? Describe the panel ordering, whether arguments and options with the same custom panel name share a panel, and whether empty default panels are printed.

criteria.description: Hidden parameters are skipped. TyperArgument and TyperOption entries are collected into separate mappings, with falsey custom names falling back to Arguments and Options respectively; a shared custom title therefore does not merge the two parameter categories.

Argument panels are emitted before option panels. Within each category the default panel is attempted first, followed by custom panels in mapping insertion order, even if a custom panel was encountered before the default.

For a group, subcommands are processed after parameter panels; unresolved or hidden commands are skipped, falsey panel names fall back to Commands, and the default command panel is attempted before custom command panels in mapping insertion order.
Empty default panel calls do not produce visible empty panels: parameter panels print only if options_rows is nonempty, and command panels print only if the constructed table has rows.

material_error_examples: Matching custom titles merge arguments and options into one panel.
Custom panels always print before the corresponding default panel.
A hidden command is still displayed if it has a custom panel name.
The Arguments, Options, and Commands default panels are printed even when they contain no entries.

novelty.distinct_mechanism: Rich presentation partitioning and empty-panel suppression, not subcommand declaration-order implementation or nested help-text precedence.

questions.question: When using CliRunner.isolation, how do runner-level and per-call environment overrides combine, and what does an override of None do? Explain how visible versus hidden prompts consume and echo supplied input, how ANSI stripping honors the isolation color setting versus an explicit color argument, and which changed process state is restored even if the context body raises.

criteria.description: Environment overrides begin with a copy of runner.env and per-call entries replace matching keys. Isolation saves each affected original value, removes keys whose override is None, and assigns the other overrides.

Visible input writes the prompt, reads one supplied line, removes trailing CR/LF, and echoes the resulting value plus a newline. Hidden input writes the prompt plus a newline and reads a line with trailing CR/LF removed without echoing its value. Explicit flush operations and exhausted-input behavior are optional supporting details.
The replacement ANSI-strip helper uses the isolation color setting only when its own color argument is None; an explicit argument overrides that default, with stripping being the negation of color.

The finally block restores affected environment keys to their original values or absence, all three standard streams, visible and hidden prompt helpers, the getchar helper, both ANSI-strip helpers, and the previous forced terminal width, including when the context body raises.

material_error_examples: A None environment override is converted to the literal string None.
Per-call environment overrides replace the entire runner environment mapping instead of merging it.
Hidden input echoes the supplied secret just like visible input.
An explicit color argument is ignored in favor of the isolation default.
Process-global state is restored only after a successful context body.

questions.question: When completion is installed explicitly for zsh with a supplied program name but no completion-variable name, what variable and script names are chosen? Explain the changes to the user startup file and completion script, including repeated installation, an existing unrelated zstyle customization, and the naming of the generated completion function.

criteria.description: With no complete_var supplied, the installer constructs _<PROGRAM>_COMPLETE by replacing hyphens with underscores and uppercasing the supplied program name; the explicit zsh branch calls the zsh installer. The installer return value is not required.

The zsh installer reads an existing ~/.zshrc, appends the exact fpath/compinit initialization line only when absent, and adds its menu-select style only if the substring zstyle is absent altogether. An unrelated existing zstyle therefore suppresses the default style; startup contents are stripped and rewritten with one trailing newline.

The completion file is ~/.zfunc/_<program-name>, its parent directory is created as needed, and write_text overwrites the generated script rather than appending another copy on repeated installation. The helper return value is not required.

The function identifier is _<sanitized-name>_completion, where hyphens become underscores and remaining characters outside ASCII letters, digits, and underscore are removed. The zsh template uses that identifier for its function and compdef binding, while retaining the original program name and the selected completion variable in the generated script.

material_error_examples: Repeated installation appends another completion script to ~/.zfunc instead of overwriting it.
The zsh menu-select style is added unless that exact style line already exists, regardless of unrelated zstyle configuration.
The script filename uses the uppercased sanitized completion-variable name.
Repeated installation unconditionally duplicates the fpath initialization line.

novelty.distinct_mechanism: Persistent zsh startup/script installation and identifier generation, not interpretation of incoming completion action_shell instructions.
